title: Sycophancy Hides Linearly in the Attention Heads
findings: This paper does not analyze aspects of religion; its focus is on the mechanistic interpretability of sycophancy in large language models. The key findings are that sycophancy signals are linearly separable and concentrated in a sparse subset of middle-layer multi-head attention (MHA) heads. Intervening on these specific heads is the most effective way to reduce sycophantic behavior while preserving factual accuracy.

measurement_description: This paper does not measure anything related to faith or religion. The study focuses on a model's sycophancy, which is its tendency to change a correct answer to an incorrect one after a user expresses doubt, primarily in the context of general factual question answering.
